The aim is to replace standardized confection sizes with on-demand fabrication of custom-tailored, custom-fitted clothing covering the full diversity range of human shapes.", "notes": "FILTER: euroSciVoc textiles subtree (engineering and technology/materials engineering/textiles) intersected with fundingScheme='ERC-COG'. Path matched with LIKE '%/textiles%' because euroSciVocPath carries NO leading slash. Executed this pass: 7 survivors (the textiles subtree alone holds 295 projects across SME/RIA/IA/MSCA, so the ERC-COG restriction is what produces an enumerable, readable set). ADJUDICATION (exhaustive - S=7 <= 20, every survivor's objective and report teaser read via get_project_text; scoped pooled search run for retrievability/rank matrix only, not for gold selection): 101003104 MYCLOTH IN - its objective names the 'fast fashion' approach, states nearly 50% of manufactured garments are destined for landfill or incineration, and answers it with geometric modeling/optimization of personalized, custom-fitted, fabricable garments (digital garment shape space, algorithmic personalization, on-demand fabrication instead of standardized confection sizes). 648763 INTERACT OUT - liquid-crystal electrospun non-woven textiles for wearable sensors and soft robotics; no waste or fast-fashion concern. 682711 PENELOPE OUT - weaving as technical mode of existence, ancient Greek epistemology and the history of coding. 726195 RE-FASHIONING OUT - Renaissance popular dress 1550-1650, textile/dye analysis and historical reconstruction; historical fashion, not fast-fashion waste. 771288 TextileLab OUT - household labour, livelihood and consumption in the 1750-1990 relocation of cotton manufacturing; economic history, no waste argument. 819458 PoliticsOfPatents OUT - clothing patents in Espacenet read as citizenship claims. 101002711 BODYinTRANSIT OUT - sensory-driven body transformation experiences and mental body representations; mentions fashion design only as an application area. Non-embedding sweep over all 7 survivors' objective + report (summary/workPerformed/finalResults/teaser) for 'fast fashion', 'landfill', 'overproduction' returned MYCLOTH alone (obj + waste terms), all six others empty - confirming the exhaustive read. FILTER-DISCRIMINATION (unscoped pooled k=10 with the same question): many projects satisfy the textual ask but fail the ERC-COG filter, e.g. 646226 Trash-2-Cash (IA, textiles-tagged; design-driven regeneration of textile fibre waste into fashion products, 'decrease landfill volumes'), 101003906 SCIRT (IA, textiles-tagged; textile-to-textile recycling for a more circular fashion system, noting less than 1% of textile waste is recycled into new fibres), 101000632 HEREWEAR (IA, textiles-tagged; circular locally-produced clothing from bio-based waste), plus REFREAM (RIA), RESYNTEX/TCBL/New Cotton (IA). All seven carry the same textiles euroSciVoc tag, so it is precisely the fundingScheme='ERC-COG' half of the filter that excludes them - the filter is load-bearing and the question is not a vector question in disguise. TEXT SIDE: no stored column records how a project proposes to change garment design and production; the answer exists only in MYCLOTH's objective text. TERM_STYLE exact-term: the question reuses 'fast fashion', 'waste' and 'garments' verbatim from MYCLOTH's objective, and the scoped rank matrix agrees - MYCLOTH is lexical rank 2 (real term overlap), hybrid_rerank rank 1. Note that RE-FASHIONING outranks MYCLOTH in lexical/dense/hybrid (rank 1) on surface 'fashion' vocabulary, so the question is not solved by top-1 retrieval alone."}

CHECKLIST: APPROVE (all drafter-owned items PASS; NO-TELEGRAPH / NEAR-DUPLICATE / GENERIC-FACT deferred to reviewer)

EVIDENCE:

FILTER (executed this pass, true count 7):
SELECT DISTINCT p.id, p.acronym FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/textiles%' AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-COG' ORDER BY p.id
| id | acronym | title |
|---|---|---|
| 648763 | INTERACT | Intelligent Non-woven Textiles and Elastomeric Responsive materials by Advancing liquid Crystal Technology |
| 682711 | PENELOPE | A study of weaving as technical mode of existence |
| 726195 | RE-FASHIONING | Re-fashioning the Renaissance: Popular Groups, Fashion and the Material and Cultural Significance of Clothing in Europe, 1550-1650 |
| 771288 | TextileLab | Race to the bottom? Family labour, household livelihood and consumption in the relocation of global cotton manufacturing, ca. 1750-1990 |
| 819458 | PoliticsOfPatents | Politics of Patents: Re-imagining citizenship via clothing inventions 1820 - 2020 |
| 101002711 | BODYinTRANSIT | Sensory-driven Body Transformation Experiences On-the-move |
| 101003104 | MYCLOTH | Sustainable Algorithmic Modeling of Personalized Garments |

GOLD - 101003104 MYCLOTH, verbatim from its project.objective:
"In addition, the "fast fashion" approach of selling large volumes of garments at very low prices and changing collections very frequently leads to significant waste of natural and human resources: according to recent research nearly 50% of all manufactured garments are imminently destined for landfill or incineration. A fundamental, radical change is required to the way clothes are designed, manufactured and delivered to consumers, generating value and attachment via quality instead of quantity and curbing toxic overproduction. The goal of this project is to bring transformative technological advances in geometric modeling and optimization of personalized, custom-fitted and fabricable garments in order to crucially support this change. To reach our goals, we must break away from traditional shape representations and modeling pipelines and develop a dedicated mathematical and algorithmic foundation for digital cloth and garment modeling. Our envisioned theoretical basis of the digital garment shape space will on the one hand facilitate a novel interactive modeling framework to support apparel designers in the creative task of template garment design in a reality-faithful manner, and on the other hand serve as the enabling foundation for automated, algorithmic garment personalization to perfectly fit any human body model. In stark contrast to current practice of standardized confection sizes, our framework will enable on-demand fabrication of custom-tailored clothing while being inclusive of the full diversity range of human shapes."
(MYCLOTH has no published report row; the objective is the whole evidence.)

REJECTED SURVIVORS (each read in full, one-line reason with its own text):
- 648763 INTERACT - OUT. "The extreme responsiveness of LCs is transferred to a non-woven textile by incorporating the LC in the fiber core, yielding a smart flexible mat with sensory function" - smart-materials engineering for wearables; no fast-fashion or waste motivation.
- 682711 PENELOPE - OUT. "The PENELOPE project builds on the hypothesis that there was a significant but tacit contribution of textile technology involved in the advent of science in ancient Greece" - epistemology of weaving, not garment production.
- 726195 RE-FASHIONING - OUT. "This study of Renaissance dress offers a better understanding of how fashion developed at popular levels of society in Europe, 1550-1650" - historical dress study; the word "fashion" is surface overlap only.
- 771288 TextileLab - OUT. "Its main question is to what extent, and how, gender divisions of work, households' multiple livelihood strategies, and local consumption patterns have influenced the continuation and disappearance of textile manufacturing over time and space?" - labour/relocation history, no waste argument.
- 819458 PoliticsOfPatents - OUT. "It focuses on clothing patents in Espacenet, the European Patent Office's free online database" - citizenship studies via patents.
- 101002711 BODYinTRANSIT - OUT. "The aim of this ERC-funded project BODYinTRANSIT is to establish a new fundamental knowledge base for individualised sensorial manipulation of body perceptions" - fashion design named only as a downstream application area.

NON-EMBEDDING SWEEP over the 7 survivors' objective + report for 'fast fashion', 'landfill', 'overproduction': MYCLOTH = obj + waste terms; INTERACT, PENELOPE, RE-FASHIONING, TextileLab, PoliticsOfPatents, BODYinTRANSIT = all empty.

DISCRIMINATION COUNTER-EXAMPLES (unscoped pooled k=10 hits that satisfy the textual ask but fail the filter; scheme and textiles-tag confirmed by SQL):
- 646226 Trash-2-Cash, IA, textiles-tagged: "growing problems with paper fibre waste from the paper industry and textile fibre waste ... will be solved through design-driven innovation ... decrease landfill volumes and energy consumption".
- 101003906 SCIRT, IA, textiles-tagged: "less than 1% of textile waste is recycled into new textile fibres... SCIRT aims to support systemic innovation towards a more circular fashion system".
- 101000632 HEREWEAR, IA, textiles-tagged: "innovates with a holistic, systemic approach towards the creation of an EU market for locally-produced circular textiles and clothing made from bio-based waste".
- Also outside the filter: 825647 REFREAM (RIA), 641942 RESYNTEX (IA), 646133 TCBL (IA), 101000559 New Cotton (IA). All seven carry the textiles euroSciVoc tag, so fundingScheme='ERC-COG' is what excludes them.

SCOPED RANK MATRIX (search over the 7 survivors, k=10, index be84cbad9182): MYCLOTH lexical 2 / dense 2 / hybrid 2 / hybrid_rerank 1; RE-FASHIONING 1/1/1/2; TextileLab 6/3/3/3; PoliticsOfPatents 5/4/4/4; BODYinTRANSIT 3/null/7/5; INTERACT 4/null/5/7; PENELOPE 7/null/6/6.

WHY-GOOD:
The question discriminates two things at once: a system must apply a scheme+taxonomy filter it cannot get from text (seven ERC-COG textiles projects out of 295 in the textiles subtree), and then read which of those seven actually argues from fast-fashion waste - a theme that dominates the corpus outside the filter (Trash-2-Cash, SCIRT, HEREWEAR, RESYNTEX, New Cotton and others all IA/RIA), so pure vector retrieval lands on circular-economy consortia rather than on MYCLOTH. It fills the hybrid coverage gaps of a fundingScheme filter (hyb-01 uses a date filter, hyb-03 a funding-percentile filter) and a euroSciVoc engineering/materials topic branch, at exact-term style. L1/filter-read is honest: exactly one survivor satisfies the textual requirement, and the answer is a single fact read from that one project's objective, not synthesized across projects.

HISTORY:
- Startup: get_bank_questions("hybrid") returned hyb-01 and hyb-03 - no collision with a fundingScheme filter on textiles. Retrieval probe succeeded (index be84cbad9182). get_schema_docs() returned sd2 / f8c001e8cc8f.
- Drift check: re-ran the candidate's filter SQL verbatim; still 7 survivors, no drift.
- Read all 7 survivors (objective + report teaser) in one call. The candidate block's framing was too open for an L1 single-fact read, so the textual ask was sharpened to the fast-fashion-waste motivation, which exactly one survivor (MYCLOTH) carries.
- Concern raised and resolved during drafting: a textual predicate as specific as PENELOPE's "penemorphism" or PoliticsOfPatents' "Espacenet" would have made the filter decorative. The fast-fashion-waste predicate was chosen precisely because it is a crowded corpus theme outside the filter.
- Verification: scoped pooled search for retrievability/term-style; unscoped pooled search for discrimination; SQL check that counter-examples are textiles-tagged non-ERC-COG; SQL term sweep over survivors. filter_sql executed verbatim in final form after the question text was fixed.
- Notable finding kept as a feature: RE-FASHIONING outranks MYCLOTH in three of four scoped conditions on surface "fashion" vocabulary, so the question cannot be answered by taking scoped rank 1.

{"question_id": "hyb-05", "text": "Among the Marie Skłodowska-Curie standard European individual fellowships (funding scheme MSCA-IF-EF-ST) classified under musicology, what do those examining how music helped shape a country's sense of nationhood set out to investigate?", "expected_route": "hybrid", "level": "L2", "subtype": "filter-synthesize", "specification": "well-specified", "term_style": "paraphrase", "gold_project_ids": [659468, 745631, 750086], "filter_evidence": {"filter_sql": "SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/musicology%' AND p.fundingScheme = 'MSCA-IF-EF-ST' ORDER BY p.id", "survivor_count": 13, "survivor_ids": [656349, 659468, 661734, 707827, 745631, 750086, 750618, 750706, 752884, 792150, 800280, 844238, 867427], "schema_docs_hash": "f8c001e8cc8f"}, "pooling_evidence": {"conditions_run": ["lexical", "dense", "hybrid", "hybrid_rerank"], "k": 10, "pooled_candidate_count": 13, "accepted": [659468, 745631, 750086], "rejected_count": 10, "index_fingerprint": "be84cbad9182", "scope_size": 13, "adjudication_mode": "exhaustive-read of all 13 survivors; the scoped pooled search (k=10, union over four conditions) surfaced 11 of the 13 and supplied the rank matrix, but every survivor was read in full and adjudicated from its text"}, "reference_answer": "Transnational Localism (659468) takes Francis Poulenc, a French composer who lived through both World Wars, as its case for asking how localised urban, suburban and rural places fed a distinctive musical and national identity, following his UK collaborations with Britten and Lennox Berkeley, his clandestine WWII activities with the BBC, and post-WWI European-American artistic exchange. GRIDAMUS (745631) sets out to build an interdisciplinary framework - historical musicology, Modern Greek Studies and ethnomusicology - for a revisionist reading of modern Greek art music since the formation of the Greek nation-state in the early 19th century (post-1830), treating 'Greekness' as something the repertory mediates rather than an essential, timeless trait. Aural Paris (750086) examines how composers, singer/songwriters, authors and filmmakers of the French Third Republic (1870-1940) - among them Aristide Bruant, Jean Cocteau, Gustave Charpentier and René Clair - turned the city's sounds into creative force and political metaphor, re-evaluating the politics of the city soundscape and its role in defining French identity. All three work outward from archival sources on one composer, repertory or city, and treat music as a place where a nation's self-image is assembled and contested rather than merely reflected.", "notes": "FILTER: euroSciVoc leaf 'musicology' (path matched with LIKE '%/musicology%' - paths carry no leading slash) intersected with fundingScheme='MSCA-IF-EF-ST' (MSCA Individual Fellowships, standard European Fellowship panel). TEXT LOAD-BEARING: no stored column encodes what a fellowship investigates, and 10 of the 13 survivors fail the textual requirement. EVIDENCE:

FILTER (executed this pass, schema_docs sd2 / f8c001e8cc8f):
SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/musicology%' AND p.fundingScheme = 'MSCA-IF-EF-ST' ORDER BY p.id
row_count = 13, truncated = false. Survivors (id | acronym): 656349 IPBMNES, 659468 Transnational Localism, 661734 PE4PPI, 707827 OXFORDCHOIRS, 745631 GRIDAMUS, 750086 Aural Paris, 750618 VRAASP, 750706 MEMORISING, 752884 INTIMAL, 792150 LadinoProverbs, 800280 DiCrEd, 844238 ClassRockED, 867427 DUEL. Musicology overall = 86 projects.

GOLD 1 - 659468, Transnational Localism, "Transnational Localism and Music after the two World Wars: the case of Francis Poulenc" (objective, verbatim):
"This project looks at the role composers played in the construction of European culture in the aftermath of two World Wars. Taking Francis Poulenc as an example of a French composer who experienced war twice, it looks at his creative responses to the wars. It prioritises the musical and cultural significance of localised urban, suburban and rural places in shaping a distinctive musical and national identity, an identity that was recognised by his contemporaries as representing a generation; it also scrutinises his international activities in pursuit of cultural and artistic co-operation, collaboration and exchange. The project includes a study of Poulenc's UK connections, using understudied archival materials to explore his collaborations with composers such as Britten and Lennox Berkeley, his presence in concert life and his clandestine WWII activities with the BBC. ... This project responds to this challenge by exploring the role of music in shaping identities on individual, generational, national and European levels."

GOLD 2 - 745631, GRIDAMUS, "Greek Identity in Art Music since the Early Nineteenth Century: Towards an Interdisciplinary Methodology" (objective, verbatim):
"This project is the first large-scale, interdisciplinary attempt to study mechanisms of national identity construction through modern Greek (post-1830) art music. It has two primary objectives: a) to develop an interdisciplinary methodological framework for the analysis of Greek art music drawing on historical musicology, Modern Greek Studies and ethnomusicology; and b) to offer a revisionist study of Greek art music - a repertory that remains to be investigated in the depth it merits - by exploring the ways in which it has mediated Greek identity during the period since the formation of the Greek nation-state in the early 19th century. Traditionally, the issue of 'Greekness' - a perceived national character or identity - in music has been analysed with respect to the question of the assumed 'continuity' of Greek history and culture since antiquity... Yet, such treatment of national identity is essentialising and self-exoticising."
(report finalResults, verbatim): "GRIDAMUS is an important contribution to scientific enquiries that have challenged the understanding of national identity and, more generally, Greek identity as a monolithic and atemporal entity."

GOLD 3 - 750086, Aural Paris, "Aural Paris: The Changing Identities of The City of Sound in Music, Film and Literature, 1870-1940." (objective, verbatim):
"This project examines the creative assimilation of the city of Paris into the music, film and literature of the French Third Republic (1870-1940). ... the study, which analyses how singer/songwriters, composers, authors and filmmakers -such as Victor Fournel, Aristide Bruant, Jean Cocteau, Gustave Charpentier, René Clair and Pierre Mac Orlan- used the city and its sounds as creative force and political metaphor. ... The project allows us to re-evaluate the politics of the city soundscape and its role in defining French identity."
(report summary, verbatim): "The changing landscape of the city is the background to this project, which considered how the sonic fabric of the urban context was conceptualised as a defining characteristic of Frenchness."

SURVIVORS THAT FAIL THE TEXTUAL REQUIREMENT (10 of 13): 656349 IPBMNES (pedestrian flow modelling and evacuation simulation - no music); 661734 PE4PPI (peer ethnography, young people's sexual health services); 707827 OXFORDCHOIRS ("collective identities and (sometimes contested) cultures of collegiate choirs at University of Oxford" - collegiate, not national); 750618 VRAASP (archaeoacoustics and VR of "ancient or historical spaces"); 750706 MEMORISING ("relationships between memory, rock art and acoustics"); 752884 INTIMAL (telematic "relational listening" system with nine Colombian migrant women); 792150 LadinoProverbs ("first peremiological study of the Sephardic tradition from Serbia and Bosnia"); 800280 DiCrEd (digital critical edition of Verdi's French Macbeth); 844238 ClassRockED ("ideals and markers of social class ... within ... a rock music school in the US Midwest"); 867427 DUEL ("first comparative study of poetic duelling across the Mediterranean").

FILTER-DISCRIMINATION COUNTER-EXAMPLES (satisfy the text, fail the filter):
- SQL sweep (executed): SELECT DISTINCT p.id, p.acronym, p.fundingScheme, p.title FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID=p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/musicology%' AND p.fundingScheme <> 'MSCA-IF-EF-ST' AND (lower(p.objective) LIKE '%national identity%' OR lower(p.objective) LIKE '%nationalism%' OR lower(p.objective) LIKE '%patriotic%' OR lower(p.objective) LIKE '%nation-state%') -> 2 rows: 833366 CLEFNI (MSCA-IF), 101018743 Transopera (ERC-ADG).
- CLEFNI 833366 (objective, verbatim): "During the 19th century, several music and choral societies arose in Europe, giving rise to a choral movement that fostered not only communal singing, but also patriotic feelings. In Switzerland, this movement involved several men's choirs that had a strong liberal and patriotic character. ... With its songs and festivals, the Swiss choral movement became a crucial element in this integration process."
- Transopera 101018743 (report summary, verbatim): "our work challenges conventional and pre-conceived ideas about music as being organised principally according to national categories. Showing how music, during the age of nationalism, served building bridges between national and religious communities..."
- Unscoped retrieval on the final wording also returned MUSICOL 834195 (ERC-ADG, "the musical dimension of the French empire ... colonial identities") and EURJAZZ 800242 (MSCA-IF, "the role of music in shaping identities at European level").

SCOPED RANK MATRIX (final wording, condition=pooled, k=10, scope = the 13 survivors, index be84cbad9182) - lexical / dense / hybrid / hybrid_rerank:
659468 Transnational Localism 2/1/1/1 (gold); 844238 ClassRockED 1/5/3/3; 707827 OXFORDCHOIRS 4/2/2/6; 745631 GRIDAMUS 5/3/4/2 (gold); 750086 Aural Paris 3/4/5/4 (gold); 792150 LadinoProverbs 10/-/-/5; 750618 VRAASP 6/6/7/10; 752884 INTIMAL 7/7/6/8; 800280 DiCrEd 8/-/9/7; 750706 MEMORISING -/8/8/-; 867427 DUEL 9/-/10/9. (11 of 13 survivors appear in the union; 656349 and 661734 do not.)

TERM-STYLE SQL CHECK (executed): over the 13 survivors, lower(objective) LIKE '%nationhood%' = 0 hits and lower(summary||teaser) LIKE '%nationhood%' = 0 hits; lower(objective) LIKE '%national identity%' = 2 hits (659468, 745631).

WHY-GOOD:
The question discriminates on a property no column stores - whether a musicology fellowship treats music as a maker of national self-image - and only 3 of the 13 enumerated survivors qualify, with a genuine near-miss (OXFORDCHOIRS, collegiate rather than national identity) that punishes topic-level matching. It fills open coverage axes: the first humanities/arts topic in the hybrid ladder, the first funding-scheme filter, and the first hybrid filter-synthesize/paraphrase cell. The L2/filter-synthesize label is honest because |gold| = 3 sits inside the [2,4] bound and the answer is one integrated statement drawn across three fellowships; paraphrase is honest because "nationhood" appears nowhere in any survivor's text.

HISTORY:
- Startup: get_bank_questions("hybrid") returned hyb-01 and hyb-03 - no collision. Retrieval probe succeeded (index be84cbad9182). get_schema_docs() returned sd2 / f8c001e8cc8f.
- Drift check: the candidate's count SQL re-executed to 13 survivors; enumeration returned all 13 ids.
- Exhaustive read of all 13 survivors confirmed euroSciVoc noise: IPBMNES (pedestrian modelling) and PE4PPI (sexual-health ethnography) are tagged musicology but are not music research.
- Theme selection: three candidate textual requirements were visible - archaeoacoustics (|gold| = 2), oral/intangible heritage (weakly coherent), music as maker of national self-image (3 survivors). The last was chosen for its mid-bound gold count, sharp in-filter near-miss, and out-of-filter counter-examples.
- One failed SQL (parser error on a CASE WHEN term-style probe) was fixed and re-run, giving the 0/13 "nationhood" result.
- Question wording was edited after the first pass (added the explicit scheme code, "forge"->"shape", "study"->"investigate"). All retrieval verification was re-run against the exact final wording; the filter-discrimination claim was additionally grounded in a wording-independent SQL sweep.
- The exact filter_sql recorded in the entry was executed once more at the end of the pass and returned the same 13 ids.
